claim.why_it_matters: Flowchart flattened; its boxes are rendered as a 2-column table with a header row, and both loop-backs (to Condition-2 and to Condition-1) are lost.

verdict.reasoning: Rendered printed page 874 (PDF p898) at 300 dpi. Figure D.12 is a flowchart: Entrance -> Set id-2 to FROM -> Set id-5 to FROM -> Condition-1 (True -> Exit; False -> Condition-2); Condition-2 False -> Execute specified set of statements -> Augment id-5 with BY -> loop back into Condition-2; Condition-2 True -> Augment id-2 with BY -> Set id-5 to FROM -> loop back into Condition-1. The pdf_says summary matches the printed edges. The markdown keeps every box label, but it puts the four lower boxes into a 2-column table. The first row of that table is a header holding half of each of two boxes, so box text is split across rows. It carries no arrows, so neither loop-back appears, and the True/False labels hang loose with nothing to say which branch leads where. The figure's content is its control flow, which is the nesting of the two VARYING loops, and that cannot be recovered from the markdown. This is a genuine loss of figure content, not just formatting. The figure is in informative Annex D, so the loss is structural, not normative. The markdown_says quote matches the transcription exactly.
